patientGoals: The sleeping pill. I don't think it even works anymore, and I hate feeling like this in the mornings. I just want to feel clear again.

objection: Abruptly layering a benzodiazepine taper simultaneously with discontinuation of diphenhydramine (also sedating/anticholinergic) risks unmasking withdrawal-related insomnia, anxiety, and rebound symptoms without a clear stabilization sequence, potentially causing the patient to feel worse before better and undermining trust in the plan. The plan should explicitly sequence which agent is tapered first (typically benzodiazepine slow taper while holding other CNS-active drugs steady) to avoid confounding withdrawal symptoms with cascade reversal effects.

steps.note: Baseline dose. Begin CBT-I/sleep hygiene counselling before or alongside taper initiation; do not change dose yet.
25% reduction from starting dose. Achievable using a 0.5 mg tablet plus half of a 1 mg tablet, or three 0.25 mg quarter-tablets if available.
25% reduction (now at 50% of starting dose - the threshold for switching taper method). Standard 0.5 mg tablet strength, no splitting required.

Below 50% of starting dose - now applying 12.5% reduction steps of the original dose per algorithm. Achievable by quartering a 0.5 mg tablet (three quarters) or via oral liquid formulation (e.g., 2 mg/mL) for accuracy.
12.5% reduction step. Achievable as half of a 0.5 mg tablet.
12.5% reduction step. Achievable as one quarter of a 0.5 mg tablet, or preferably via liquid formulation given the small quantity involved.

steps.dose: 0.125 mg on most nights, with 1-2 planned drug-free nights per week
steps.note: Per algorithm guidance, at the lowest achievable tablet dose switch from further splitting to planned drug-free nights rather than attempting doses below 0.125 mg.

steps.dose: 0.125 mg with increasing number of drug-free nights (progressing toward 0)
steps.note: Gradually increase drug-free nights every 1-2 weeks as tolerated until fully off. Given 9 years of use, this final phase may need to extend over additional weeks to months - do not rush; slow further if withdrawal symptoms emerge. Never stop abruptly from any dose.
